claims.text: China vs Sudan: The Childhood Vaccine Gap
claims.support: China immunization rate is 97% (CHN), Sudan immunization rate is 39% (SDN)
Child immunization, DPT, measures percentage of children 12-23 months receiving DPT vaccinations

claims.text: A global comparison of childhood DPT immunization rates between China and Sudan using World Bank data.
claims.support: Indicator SH.IMM.IDPT from World Bank comparing CHN (97%) and SDN (39%)

claims.text: In China, 97% of toddlers get basic DPT vaccines. In Sudan, it's 39%.
claims.support: China value is 97.0%, Sudan value is 39.0%

claims.text: China protects nearly all its young children against diphtheria, pertussis, and tetanus.
Sudan is the world's lowest, where most toddlers lack full protection.
claims.support: Sudan rank is 189 out of 189 (lowest), value is 39% (below 50%)

claims.text: Full protection requires 3 doses of vaccine during infancy.
claims.support: Definition: A child is considered adequately immunized against diphtheria, pertussis (or whooping cough), and tetanus (DPT) after receiving three doses of vaccine.

claims.text: That gives China 2.5 times the immunization rate of Sudan.
claims.support: China is 97% and Sudan is 39%; 97 / 39 = 2.487 (approximately 2.5 times)

claims.text: Across all nations, the median country sits at 91%.
claims.support: Many entities have 91% (e.g., BRA, BFA, FIN, KEN, MWI, NLD, NZL, SEN, SLE, ZMB, ZWE), representing the middle value of the distribution

claims.text: How high is childhood DPT immunization in your country?
claims.support: Question referencing the indicator universe of mapped countries and territories

claims.text: HOW PROTECTED ARE TODDLERS? DPT Immunization Rate, World Bank
claims.support: Indicator title and theme matching World Bank SH.IMM.IDPT
